McHenry County Tax Lien Sale: Earn 9% Returns Every Six Months

Click Here to Get Dustin Hahn’s Tax Lien and Deed FREE Mini-Course

Investing in McHenry County, Illinois tax liens is a great way to secure high returns, offering up to 9% every six months over a period of 2.5 to 3 years. If you’re seeking a lucrative, low-risk investment, McHenry County’s annual tax lien sale could be your opportunity to earn significant returns while potentially acquiring property at a fraction of its value. Start by following this complete guide.

What Are Tax Lien Certificates?

Tax lien certificates are legal claims sold by the county on properties with unpaid property taxes. When you purchase a tax lien certificate, you’re essentially paying the delinquent taxes on behalf of the property owner. In return, you earn interest on that payment until the owner repays the taxes.

Here’s how it works:

  • Example: If you pay $1,000 in unpaid taxes, you could earn $90 every six months at a 9% interest rate, which compounds semi-annually.
  • Redemption Period: If the property owner does not redeem the lien within the 2-3 year redemption period, you may petition to take ownership of the property for just the back taxes and fees.

Why Invest in McHenry County Tax Liens?

McHenry County, established in 1836, is a historically rich area named after Major William McHenry, a Blackhawk War hero.

The annual tax lien auction features an appealing 9% interest rate that bidders actively reduce during the event. If a buyer redeems the lien within a few months, you still receive the full 9% penalty, making it a high-reward, low-risk investment.

How to Start Investing

Follow these steps to begin investing in McHenry County’s tax lien auction:

1. Research and Understand Local Laws

Before investing, it’s crucial to understand the legal framework governing tax lien sales in McHenry County. Each jurisdiction has its own rules, so familiarize yourself with local regulations by visiting the McHenry County Treasurer’s Office website.

2. Visit the McHenry County Treasurer’s Website

Visit the treasurer’s website to stay updated on the latest tax sale announcements, rules, and registration details. Understanding how the sale operates is key to making informed investment decisions.

3. Register for the Auction

To participate in the auction, you must register in advance:

  • Registration Fee: To register, you must pay a fee of $500, and you can choose to pay an optional $200 fee for the tax sale list..
  • Deadline: Ensure you complete your registration by the first week of November.

4. Attend the Auction in Person

  • Location: They hold Auctions at the McHenry County Administration Building, located at 667 Ware Road, Woodstock, IL.
  • Bidding Process: The auction follows a bid-down process, starting at 9% interest and going down to 0%. The lowest bidder wins, earning the full penalty upon redemption by the property owner.

Pro Tips Investors In McHenry County

  • Register Early: The law requires registration. Ensure you complete it by early November to secure your place in the auction.
  • Understand the Bidding Process: The interest rate begins at 9% and is bid down, so be prepared to participate actively.
  • Stay Updated: Regularly check the Treasurer’s website for updates on tax lien auctions, sale schedules, and rules.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Q: What happens if no one bids on a tax lien?

A: The Trustee automatically purchases the taxes at the 9% interest rate if no bids are placed.

Q: Can I attend the auction online?

A: Currently, McHenry County holds the auction in person at the Administration Building in Woodstock, IL. For updates on possible online participation, check with the Treasurer’s Office.

Q: What happens if the property owner redeems the property?

A: If the property owner redeems the lien, you will receive your investment back along with the interest rate from your winning bid.

Q: Can I take ownership of the property?

A: If the property owner does not redeem the lien within the 2-3 year redemption period, you can petition to take ownership of the property by acquiring a tax deed.
